summary: Code review PASS. All three root-cause fixes are well-implemented and idiomatic: (1) api.config.notesDisplay.get stub correctly prevents the Promise.all hang that was the primary regression. (2) afterEach(() => { restoreTimers(); }) guarantees timer restoration even on mid-test assertion failures — the unconditional placement is correct and robust. (3) Map<number, Function> (_pendingTimers) replacing the single _timerId counter is the correct fix for clearTimeout semantics — the ID-to-callback mapping and conditional _pendingDebounce null-out on lines 144-151 are architecturally sound. No blocking issues found. One low-priority documentation-forward note raised about the scrollIntoView stub restoration guard.

comments.note: The _nextTimerId seed value of 2000 (line 137) is a magic number chosen to avoid collision with real timer IDs. A brief comment explaining this intent (e.g., '// Start IDs high to avoid collisions with any real jsdom timer IDs') would improve future maintainability.

restoreTimers() (lines 172-177) correctly restores globalThis.setTimeout/clearTimeout and clears _pendingTimers, but does not reset _originalSetTimeout/_originalClearTimeout to null after restoring. A double-call is harmless (the original function would simply be re-assigned again), but resetting the sentinels to null after restoration would make the guard conditions on lines 173-174 more precise.

[documentation-forward] The scrollIntoView stub restoration guard at lines 166-169 of notes-collected.test.mjs merits a clarifying comment. After the first render() call, origScrollIntoView will always be the no-op stub installed in that same render() invocation (not the original jsdom prototype method), so the restore on lines 167-169 is effectively a no-op after test 1. A comment explaining this — e.g., '// origScrollIntoView will be our own stub after the first render; the restore is a no-op but kept for symmetry' — would prevent future confusion for contributors.

No blocking or architectural issues found. The Map-based _pendingTimers pattern is the correct idiomatic approach for multi-ID timer tracking in test stubs. The clearTimeout conditional on line 147 (_pendingDebounce === _pendingTimers.get(id)) correctly handles the case where a newer timer has already replaced the debounce reference.
